items.markdown:
Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) are `international technical standards that explain how to make digital content accessible for people with disabilities`.[[1]](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/)[[2]](https://transportation.libguides.com/c.php?g=859129&p=7249636)

### The Four POUR Principles

WCAG guidelines follow four core principles, often called POUR:[[1]](https://www.wcag.com/resource/what-is-wcag/)

- **Perceivable:** Users must be able to identify content with their senses. Provide alt text for images and captions for videos.
- **Operable:** Users must be able to navigate the interface. Ensure full keyboard navigation and avoid content that causes seizures.
- **Understandable:** Text and operation must be clear. Write readable content and make forms predictable.
- **Robust:** Content must work reliably with various assistive technologies, like screen readers.[[1]](https://www.ada.gov/resources/web-guidance/)[[2]](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/Guides/Understanding_WCAG)[[3]](https://www.wcag.com/resource/what-is-wcag/)

### Conformance Levels
Success criteria are categorized into three levels:[[1]](https://transportation.libguides.com/c.php?g=859129&p=7249636)

- **Level A:** The bare minimum level of accessibility.
- **Level AA:** The standard target for most legal compliance (such as the ADA), requiring a 4.5:1 text color contrast ratio.
- **Level AAA:** The highest and most strict level of enhancement, which is rarely required in full.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Web_Content_Accessibility_Guidelines)[[2]](https://www.wcag.com/resource/what-is-wcag/)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h5NFovz5Mpc&t=9)

### Versions

- **WCAG 2.0 & 2.1:** Widely established stable versions. Level AA under 2.1 is the common legal benchmark.
- **WCAG 2.2:** The latest stable release, adding criteria focused on cognitive, low vision, and mobile needs while remaining fully backward-compatible.
- **WCAG 3.0:** Currently in development as a future draft standard.[[1]](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/Guides/Understanding_WCAG)[[2]](https://transportation.libguides.com/c.php?g=859129&p=7249636)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=h5NFovz5Mpc&t=9)[[4]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=PdQwY5P1Gso&t=263)[[5]](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/)

Learn more about the core rules at the [W3C WCAG Overview](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/).[[1]](https://www.w3.org/WAI/standards-guidelines/wcag/)If you'd like, let me know:
